_about: The contested issues the Positions page groups voices under. An issue with a headline shows that Overview headline's cited text and links its sections; one without names its own sections and an optional link. Topics pick the media items that count as voices on it. Titles are labels, not claims about the bill. An issue may list disputes: one question, the bill passages it turns on (located and cited by tools/build.py), and the outside readings (data/takes.json) on each side. A side with no reading shows as none found; the page does not pick a winner.

disputes.question: Must an agency still consult Tribes?

passages.text: may consult with any applicable State Historic Preservation Officers, Tribal Historic Preservation Officers, Indian tribes
shall seek, discuss, as appropriate, and incorporate, as applicable, information from each applicable State Historic Preservation Officer, Tribal Historic Preservation Officer, Indian tribe
means an identifiable geographic location or feature at which an event of continuing religious or cultural significance to a living community occurred

disputes.question: What happens when a Tribe does not answer in 30 days?

passages.text: fails to respond within 30 days of receipt of a request for review of any report or finding by the applicable Federal official, the applicable Federal official shall proceed

disputes.question: Can Interior take over a Tribal preservation office?

passages.text: the Secretary shall assume all or part of the functions of the Tribal Historic Preservation Officer

disputes.question: Can an agency set aside harm to a sacred place?

passages.text: in the sole discretion of the Federal official and as otherwise allowed by law, other considerations outweigh

disputes.question: Can a court stop a project that skipped the review?

passages.text: the only remedy the court may order is to remand, without vacatur or issuance of an injunction

disputes.question: Is the new Tribal money real?

passages.text: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out this subsection $20,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2030

disputes.question: Are Tribes better off with the bill or with the administration's draft rule?
disputes.note: No single passage: this is about what happens if the bill fails and the Advisory Council finishes its draft rule.
